I bet my life savings Christopher Nolan is the last great director of this century.

Not because of Inception, Interstellar, or Oppenheimer.

But because he found a secret method to irresistible storytelling:

Nolan uses the Plot Map Technique to visualize his storyline.

He doesn’t want “constraints” to hold him back when writing the story.

So he uses this technique to help his production team visualize & then create it on screen.

Here’s how to use the Plot Map Technique:

• Make a Visual Outline (shapes, arrows, visuals)
• Emphasize Key Points (incident, climax, resolution)
• Map Character Development (impact of events/themes)

This helps keep you focused while writing.

10 Years Of Entrepreneurship (and the lesson I learned)

The hidden cost of changing your business goals every 2–3 years:
→ You break your own momentum.
→ You reset your compounding.
→ You lose the benefit of your previous experience.
→ You are forced to build new skills from scratch.
→ You spend your life starting over instead of scaling up.

The lesson for the next decade? Only play games you can see yourself playing for at least 10 years.

Why Your Product Doesn't Have To Be Perfect

The amateur mindset:
→ I need to be an industry expert first
→ I must build the "perfect" product
→ I’m waiting for the right moment to launch

The professional mindset:
→ I just need an offer to sell
→ I need to generate my first dollar
→ I will iterate and improve after I launch

Stop obsessing over perfection and start selling—you can’t make money until you have an offer on the table.

Stop Consuming And Start Writing

The most dangerous form of procrastination is the kind that feels like work. We tell ourselves we are "researching" or "learning," but when you already know the path forward, more consumption is just a distraction. Real progress happens in the seasons where you consume the least and execute the most. Stop looking for new ideas to entertain and start taking consistent action in the direction you’ve already chosen—because if your learning isn't fueling your output, it’s actively working against you.

How To Grow Your Writing Income (the volume framework)

There are only two ways to scale a writing business.
→ Scale with traffic: Market to more people by posting more often and improving your content performance.
→ Scale with upsells: Offer more products or services to your existing audience to solve new problems.

The goal is to do both—because volume, combined with an increasing lifetime value per customer, is how you turn a side hustle into a sustainable career.

4 Lessons From Scaling My Writing Agency In 2025

Results rarely follow average effort. If you want to scale your business, you have to be willing to do the work that everyone else is avoiding when the calendar year winds down. Real leadership isn't about giving orders from a distance; it's about staying in the weeds, holding space for your team, and proving that your actions carry more weight than your words. If you want a world-class team, you have to be the first one to set the standard—even when it's exhausting.

How To Get Your First 1,000 Customers

Your goal for your first 1,000 customers is to collect 1,000 testimonials.
→ Ask every single buyer for feedback
→ Learn what specific problem they were trying to fix
→ Identify the exact outcome they achieved
→ Document the language they use to describe their journey

Nothing will make you more money than talking to your customers because their words become your marketing copy and their stories become your growth engine.

The 2 Types Of Feedback Every Creator Needs

5 reasons to stop launching new products and focus on your first $1M:
→ You avoid the "shiny object" trap of jumping around
→ You turn a "good" product into a "market-leading" asset
→ You stop confusing your customers with feature bloat
→ You learn how to solve one massive problem perfectly
→ You create the cash flow needed to fund your next big idea

Once you hit $1M, then—and only then—do you start building your upsell ladder.

Building A Ghostwriting Business: Info, Software, Coaching

The secret to building a wildly profitable digital product business isn't complicated, it's about stacking offers.
→ Start with an info product that educates your audience on a core skill.
→ Create niche software that helps them implement that skill.
→ Offer high-ticket coaching or community for your power users.

This creates a compounding flywheel, turning buyers into retained users and then high-value clients.

How To Make More Money By Interviewing Clients

Most creators overcomplicate product growth, but the secret to making more money is actually tedious, not complex.

→ Email every buyer and ask where they found you
→ Ask what was missing from the product or service
→ Invite customers to a 30-minute Zoom interview
→ Record every call and document their exact phrasing
→ Use their language to rewrite your marketing copy

When you ask people how to improve, they will literally tell you exactly what to build next.
